propositions: The hardening byte-equivalence oracle invokes Pandoc twice per corpus unit (884 real production + 884 copied legacy) totaling 1,768 subprocess calls; the copied legacy process reads live mutable constants instead of immutable expected outputs, defeating oracle independence
Mutating production _PANDOC_TO format constant changes both production and legacy digests identically, proving the legacy oracle is coupled to production and fails to detect format mutations

Platform-specific Pandoc binary SHA-256 fingerprints differ between macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 for Pandoc 3.6.1; the fixture schema stored only the generating macOS hash and rejected all Linux CI runs, violating cross-platform support

Replacing the 884 copied legacy Pandoc subprocess calls with immutable expected-output lookups while preserving all 884 real production _convert calls eliminates 884 subprocesses and ~32s runtime without reducing conversion coverage
